excerpts.text:
* A compilation of sightings appeared in "Observations of Apollo 11" by *Sky and Telescope* magazine, November 1969.[[20]](#cite_note-20)
* At [Jodrell Bank Observatory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodrell_Bank_Observatory "Jodrell Bank Observatory") in the UK, the telescope was used to observe the mission, as it was used years previously for [Sputnik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sputnik "Sputnik").[[21]](#cite_note-open2-21) At the same time, Jodrell Bank scientists [were tracking](https://web.archive.org/web/20090717021523/http://www.jodrellbank.manchester.ac.uk/multimedia/audio/luna15-apollo11.html) the uncrewed Soviet spacecraft [Luna 15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luna_15 "Luna 15"), which was trying to land on the Moon.[[22]](#cite_note-22) In July 2009, Jodrell released some recordings they made.[[23]](#cite_note-23)

The NASA-independent [*Observatoire de la Côte d'Azur*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Côte_d'Azur_Observatory "Côte d'Azur Observatory"), [McDonald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McDonald_Observatory "McDonald Observatory"), [Apache Point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apache_Point_Observatory_Lunar_Laser-ranging_Operation "Apache Point Observatory Lunar Laser-ranging Operation"), and [Haleakalā](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haleakala_Observatory "Haleakala Observatory") observatories regularly use the Apollo LRRR.[[47]](#cite_note-47) Lick Observatory attempted to detect from Apollo 11's retroreflector while Armstrong and Aldrin were still on the Moon but did not succeed until August 1, 1969.[[48]](#cite_note-48) The Apollo 14 astronauts deployed a retroreflector on February 5, 1971, and McDonald Observatory detected it the same day.
The retroreflectors are proof that human-made probes reached the exact locations of the Apollo 11, 14, and 15 landing sites at exactly the same time as those missions.
